## 1. Purpose / Scope

This CRB submission presents the conceptual design for a Provider Self-Service Portal that enables Medicaid providers to manage enrollments, submit claims, check authorization status, and access remittance advices through a modern web application. The portal replaces the legacy fax-and-phone workflow that currently handles 60% of provider interactions.

- Clearly define the provider pain points and opportunity for digital self-service
- Ensure strategic alignment with Gainwell's Digital Front Door initiative
- Identify key stakeholders across state, provider, and internal teams
- Provide conceptual C4 architecture with technology stack overview
- Assess preliminary risks around provider adoption and data security
- Document HIPAA and MARS-E compliance requirements for PHI access
- Estimate costs and timeline for 9-month delivery
- Evaluate build vs. buy alternatives

## 3. Executive Summary

**Project Overview:** Build a Next.js-based Provider Self-Service Portal that enables Indiana Medicaid providers to digitally manage enrollments, submit professional and institutional claims (837P/I), check prior authorization status, and download 835 remittance advices. The portal targets 12,000 active providers currently using phone/fax for 60% of these interactions, with a goal of shifting 80% to self-service within 6 months of launch.

**Business Problem:** Provider satisfaction scores are at 3.2/5 due to slow turnaround on enrollment changes (avg 14 business days) and claims status inquiries (avg 3 calls to resolution). The state has flagged provider experience as a contract KPI for renewal in 2028. Additionally, manual processing costs $2.1M/year in call center operations.

[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/crb-good-example.md#business-process-workflow]

### Business Process Workflow

The provider workflow covers four primary journeys: (1) New enrollment submission with document upload and real-time validation, (2) Claims submission via 837P/I entry forms with pre-adjudication checks, (3) Prior authorization request and status tracking, and (4) Remittance advice download and payment reconciliation.

![Business Process Workflow](assets/crb-business-flow.svg)
page_texts.13:
[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/crb-good-example.md#conceptual-architecture-overview]

### Conceptual Architecture Overview

The solution uses a Next.js frontend deployed on EKS behind CloudFront, communicating with backend microservices via an API Gateway. The backend consists of four bounded contexts (Enrollment, Claims, Authorization, Finance) implemented as Python FastAPI services on EKS. Data flows through Amazon MSK (Kafka) for async processing and PostgreSQL (RDS) for persistence. Authentication uses Azure AD B2C federated with the state's Okta IdP.

![C4 Level 1 - System Context](assets/crb-c4-level1-context.svg)

![C4 Level 2 - Container Diagram](assets/crb-c4-level2-container.svg)
page_texts.14:
[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/crb-good-example.md#dependencies]

### Dependencies

- **Dependency 1:** IN FSSA Identity Provider (Okta) SAML federation — required for provider SSO. Impact: 4-week lead time for federation setup.
- **Dependency 2:** Existing Claims Engine API (v2.1) — required for real-time claim submission. Impact: Must be compatible with current X12 837 processing pipeline.
- **Dependency 3:** Azure AD B2C tenant provisioning — required for identity brokering. Impact: 2-week provisioning lead time.

[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/crb-good-example.md#6-risk-assessment]

## 6. Risk Assessment

| Risk | Type | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Low provider adoption of digital portal | Business | M | H | Phased rollout with incentives; provider training program; maintain phone fallback for 12 months |
| State IdP federation delays | Technical | M | M | Early engagement with FSSA IT; fallback to direct Azure AD B2C registration |
| PHI data exposure via portal | Security | L | H | WAF + OWASP top-10 hardening; pen test before launch; field-level encryption for SSN/DOB |
| Claims Engine API not supporting needed volume | Technical | L | M | Load test at 2x expected peak; circuit breaker pattern; async submission queue |

[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/crb-good-example.md#implementation-type]

### Implementation Type

**Selected:** Multi-Tenant

Justification: The Provider Portal serves a single state (Indiana) but shares the same infrastructure as other Gainwell portal deployments, reducing operational overhead by 40%. Data isolation is achieved via row-level security and dedicated schemas per tenant.
page_texts.18:
[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/crb-good-example.md#artificial-intelligence]

### Artificial Intelligence

**AI/ML Integration:** Yes

| Use Case | AI/ML Type | Data Requirements | Expected Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claims pre-adjudication suggestions | Predictive Analytics | Historical claims data (12 months) | 20% reduction in claims denials by flagging likely errors before submission |
| Document classification for enrollment | Computer Vision / NLP | Provider enrollment documents | Auto-classify uploaded docs (W-9, license, DEA) with 95% accuracy |

**AI Governance:**

- Model Training: Federated on de-identified claims data; no PII in training sets.
- Bias & Fairness: Claims suggestion model audited quarterly for demographic bias.
- Explainability: All AI suggestions include confidence score and reasoning factors.
- Data Privacy: PHI never sent to model inference; only coded claim data (CPT, ICD-10).

page_texts.20:
[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/crb-good-example.md#security-considerations]

### Security Considerations

- PII/PHI Handling: Field-level encryption for SSN, DOB; TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest.
- Access Control: RBAC with 5 roles (Admin, Biller, Credentialer, Viewer, Auditor).
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 (transit), AES-256-GCM (at rest), AWS KMS CMK.
- Audit Logging: All data access logged to CloudTrail + application audit table; 7-year retention.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- Performance: Page load < 2s (p95), API response < 500ms (p95).
- Scalability: Support 12,000 providers with 2,000 concurrent sessions.
- Availability: 99.9% during business hours (M-F 6am-10pm ET).
- Reliability: MTTR < 30 minutes for P1 incidents.

#### Alternative 1: Commercial Off-the-Shelf Portal (Salesforce Health Cloud)

- **Description:** Use Salesforce Health Cloud with Experience Cloud for provider portal.
- **Pros:** Rapid deployment (3 months); built-in CRM; state already uses Salesforce.
- **Cons:** $800K/year licensing; limited X12/NCPDP integration; vendor lock-in; customization limits.
- **Decision:** TCO 2.5x higher over 3 years; insufficient healthcare data format support; would require custom integration layer anyway.
page_texts.26:
[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/crb-good-example.md#alternative-2-extend-existing-legacy-portal]

#### Alternative 2: Extend Existing Legacy Portal

- **Description:** Add self-service features to existing JSP-based provider portal.
- **Pros:** Lower initial cost; existing user base; no migration needed.
- **Cons:** Technical debt (Java 8, Struts 1.x); no mobile support; 8-second avg page load; team refuses to maintain.
- **Decision:** Cannot meet performance NFRs; team attrition risk; state explicitly requested modern UX.
